recipes.name: Chunky Vegetarian Vegetable Soup (Fast and Easy)
ingredients_raw: 4 carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch rounds
2 baking potatoes, cut into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook and stir onion and celery in hot oil until onion is softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir garlic into the onion mixture; cook and stir until fragrant, 2 to 3 minutes more.
Pour vegetable broth and tomato sauce into pot. Simmer for about 10 minutes.
Stir carrots and potatoes through the broth. Simmer until carrots are tender, 10 to 15 minutes more.
Drop corn, edamame, okra, and kale into the soup. Continue to simmer until okra is tender, 5 to 10 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Chunky Vegetarian Vegetable Soup (Fast and Easy)
raw_recipe.description: This chunky vegetable soup is thick with potatoes, edamame, okra, kale, and corn. You won't miss the meat in this hearty stew-like meal.

review.reviewBody: This soup is absolutely delicious! You can use any vegetables you desire especially now (summer)with all of the fresh vegetables in season.

Of course I made some edits...but the basic foundation of this was perfect! 

My husband couldn't find a 15 ounce can of tomato sauce so he grabbed a 20 ounce or something close to that...and actually, it was perfect...I think it made it a little thicker and richer.

I omitted the kale, okra and edamame- my hubs doesn't care for any of that but I am sure this would have worked great either way.

I also pan seared my potatoes for a few minutes in a teaspoon of oil, with some dried thyme, dried rosemary, salt & pepper...I feel like this locks in some more flavor. I also threw in a bay leaf when the soup was cooking.

Lastly- I cooked this in my Instant Pot pressure cooker- for anyone else out there who has one, I just sauteed the onions, celery & garlic and seared the potatoes beforehand...then threw everything in the pot and used the manual button to set it for 15 minutes...then I allowed natural release for 6 minutes and released manually the rest. It was absolutely perfect...the veggies were tender without being mushy and the soup tasted great!

My hubs doesn't like soup, let alone veggies and he LOVES this.

I really love this recipe, but I only rated it four because it needs a few things to give it some real flavor. I made this to feed eight people, so I added 2 extra cups of water plus another 4 cups of vegetable broth/stock to bring the total to 10 cups (I kept the same amount of tomato sauce).
I feel that even though this recipe says 10 servings, it would only feed about 4 people with one bowl each with 4 cups of broth. 
Also, I would recommend like other reviewers have said, some seasoning. I added a touch of crushed red pepper, white pepper, salt, oregano, rosemary, thyme, turmeric, and a couple bay leaves. This adds some really smooth flavor to the broth which would otherwise just be the flavor that comes out of the box with a little bit of salt to it. 
This recipe is great because you can easily double or triple it and add as many different kinds of vegetables as you want. It can easily feed a crowd or be a small, intimate meal. It's also incredibly easy to throw together, but definitely needs help on the seasoning side!

An excellent base recipe! I tweaked it quite a bit, but it definitely helped me get started. Delicious, and I wish I hadn't halved it! 
I sauteed in broth instead of oil.
Used what I had on hand (peas, green beans, mushrooms) instead of some of the items called for (edamame, kale, okra).
Added marjoram, bay leaf, thyme, oregano, and a generous amount of freshly ground black pepper. The spices are key, if you find the base recipe bland, which I know I would have.
It's a great starter recipe. I added more spices. Instead of tomato sauce and used some leftover marinara sauce I had. Really good.

This is a great base recipe for veggie soup. I didn't have all the suggested vegetables on hand, so I only used onion, carrot, potato, and celery (which was on the ingredient list, but not in the directions, so I just added with the carrot and potato). Probably due to the lack of veggies, it did seem to need more seasoning. Another reviewer mentioned she added smoked paprika, so I added a 1/4 teaspoon myself, and that seemed just right. I also added a can of kidney beans, which made it extra tasty and filling.

I love this soup! I did make some changes; I added 6 cups of water (I like a thinner base), used kosher salt (which I believe is what the recipe intended), A LOT more fresh ground pepper, and used golden potatoes (skin on). NOTE: You should cook your carrots and potatoes prior to adding. Great with fresh baked bread =)
EXCELLENT! An upgrade on classic vegetable soup! My go to! I double the recipe and replace corn and potatoes with peas and green beans and a canned of diced tomatoes. Super healthy and yummy!
Much better than Campbell's vegetarian vegetable. I got to control the amount of sodium in this one instead of ingesting 650mg, I added only 45mg and it was still tasty!

don't know how and why, but this soup ALWAYS turns out great and flavorful even without adding salt! I always use this recipe as a base, and just change ingredients up depending on whats in my fridge at the moment :) I do use a veggie cube as well, added a half of coconut cream since i'm vegan, bunch of spices, nutritional yeast, bragg's aminos, cabbage, green beans, and freshly blended campari tomatoes instead of canned. At the end I added olives, lemon juice, paprika, cumin, chilli pepper, 2 tbs sugar, and a few squeezes of lemon. It turned out sooo good!
nice consistency and it tasted so good not much in the way of seasoning I did roast the potatoes with basil and oregano prior to using them in the soup

Update: Jan 2026. Have been using this recipe for a while now and it NEVER fails to get “Ooo YUM! 😋 “ from the crowd. Even people who don’t like “soup” or “mushy food” are impressed when using a slotted spoon over rice for a fabulous No Meat Monday. Have been looking for a good veggie soup recipe for years to match my mom’s and I can say I’ve found it. More of a stew than watery soup. When first simmering the broth and tomato sauce it seems like it will taste too tomato-ey bu all the flavors meld beautifully. Now my one-and-only vegetable stew/soup recipe. Original Post: Followed recipe exactly and it’s a combination I would never have tried together. Delicious. I used 4 tsp Better than Bullion to 4 cups water and it was plenty flavorful. Next time I will mix up the veggies and experiment with whatever I have in the pantry. Thanks for the recipe!
I used the mixed organic frozen veggies from Costco. Super easy.
So easy and quick to make, versatile. Needs add'l flavor, tho.
My husband loved it as is!
Used sweet potatoes added kombucha squash green beans cherry tomatoes soycutash and Italian seasoning bay leaf all in all versatile recipe.

This is a quick and easy soup. I added whatever I had in the refrigerator, plus a bag of organic frozen mixed vegetables because I wanted the corn, some beans and peas.
Excellent!
